copy: Most AI agent risk is visible from the outside. A Scoped Assessment starts there: passive recon of public information, no probing, no surprises.
Agents call tools, hold keys and touch production. Ask what they can reach before someone else does. Seraphim Scan runs Scoped Assessments for agent teams.
Our rule: nothing beyond passive recon happens without written client authorization and an agreed scope. Every time.
Recon. Scoped Assessment. Remediation and Retest. Fixes verified, not assumed.

Teams shipping AI agents move fast. Security reviews often lag behind. Seraphim Scan offers a Scoped Assessment in three phases: passive recon of public information, a Scoped Assessment inside an agreed scope with written authorization, then remediation support and a retest. If your roadmap includes agents with tool access, let's talk.

What does passive recon mean for us? Public information only: DNS, certificates, published docs, public repos and what your product exposes to any visitor. No probing. It is the safest way to see your outside surface the way others can.
A finding is only useful once it is fixed. Every Seraphim Scan engagement ends with a retest so your team knows the fix holds.

Building with AI agents? Three questions worth answering this quarter: What can your agents reach? What do they trust? What would you see if one misbehaved? A Scoped Assessment helps you answer all three.
Six wings. One focus. Scoped Assessments for the AI agent era.
See what the internet already sees. Passive recon first.
Find it. Fix it. Retest it.
Written authorization. Agreed scope. Clear report.
